Skin
SKIN
n. (rendering Hebrew 'ōr, Greek derma)
From Old Norse skinn, a hide. The Hebrew 'ōr means skin or hide, of man or beast, and is the word for the coats God made for Adam and Eve. It is worth noting that it is not the same word as 'ōr meaning light, though the two are spelled alike in English transliteration — a coincidence that has produced a good deal of fanciful preaching about Adam losing a garment of light, for which the Hebrew gives no warrant.

Biblical Definition

Skin in Scripture is the boundary of a man — the last thing between him and the world — and its first appearance in the Bible is a mercy purchased by death. Adam and Eve had sewn fig leaves; God replaced them: “Unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make coats of skins, and clothed them” (Gen 3:21). Something died in Eden to clothe them, and the covering God provides replaces the covering man contrives — the first sacrifice and the first gospel picture, told in a single verse without comment. Skin is also the measure of extremity in affliction. Job, stripped of everything, describes what is left of him: “My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth” (Job 19:20) — and it is out of that condition, not out of comfort, that he says I know that my redeemer liveth. Satan had earlier used skin as his cynical formula for what a man will trade to survive: “Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life” (Job 2:4), a proposition the whole book is written to disprove. Jeremiah then uses skin for the one thing about a man that cannot be altered by effort, and makes it a picture of the will in bondage to sin: “Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil” (Jer 13:23) — the answer being no, which is why regeneration must be a work of God. And when a man has been with God the change shows on the skin without his knowing it: Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone (Exo 34:29).

Webster 1828 Definition

The natural covering of animal bodies; a hide; and in Scripture the coats of skins God made for Adam, the skin of the teeth by which Job escaped, the skin the Ethiopian cannot change, and the shining skin of Moses' face.

expand to see more

SKIN, n. 1. The natural covering of animal bodies, consisting of the cuticle or scarf-skin, and the cutis or true skin.

2. A hide; the pelt of a beast, used for leather or clothing. Coats of skins. Gen. 3.

3. The exterior coat of fruits and plants; the rind.

4. A vessel made of skin, used for holding liquors; a bottle. New wine into old bottles. Matt. 9.

5. In Scripture, I am escaped with the skin of my teeth. Job 19. Can the Ethiopian change his skin? Jer. 13.

Key Scripture

Genesis 3:21 — "Unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make coats of skins, and clothed them."

Job 19:20 — "My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth."

Job 2:4 — "And Satan answered the LORD, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life."

Jeremiah 13:23 — "Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil."

Modern Corruption

Skin colour is made the fundamental category of human identity and moral standing, in place of the biblical categories of one-in-Adam and one-in-Christ; and Jeremiah's image of unchangeable skin is wrenched from its subject, which is the bondage of the will.

expand to see more

Scripture's anthropology has no category corresponding to modern race. It knows one blood — God hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth — and it locates the deep human division not between peoples but between Adam and Christ. Frameworks which make inherited skin colour the determinant of guilt, innocence, or standing therefore replace the Bible's categories rather than applying them, and they do so in both directions: the older error that used ancestry to justify contempt and bondage, and the current one that assigns moral standing by group membership. Both are answered by the same texts. There is no difference: for all have sinned; and in Christ there is neither Greek nor Jew, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free.

Jer 13:23 is separately abused, being quoted as a proverb about the futility of change in general or, worse, as though the Ethiopian's skin were the thing needing alteration. The prophet's subject is stated in the second half of his own sentence: then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil. The comparison is to habit hardened into nature, and its doctrine is the bondage of the will — that a man accustomed to evil can no more reform himself than a leopard can rearrange its spots. That is not a counsel of despair but the reason the new birth must be a work of God: except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. The principle to recover is the one Gen 3:21 sets at the very beginning: the covering a man makes for himself is inadequate, and the covering that works is one God provides at the cost of a life.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew 'ōr is skin or hide, of man or beast; it is the material of the coats God made in Eden and of the tabernacle's outer coverings. Greek derma is skin, and dermatinos means made of skin, as of John the Baptist's girdle.

expand to see more

Hebrew 'ōr (H5785) — skin, hide, leather; coats of skins (Gen 3:21) and the badgers' skins covering the tabernacle.

Hebrew bāsār (H1320) — flesh; paired with skin in Job's description of his wasted body (Job 19:20).

Hebrew qāran (H7160) — to send out rays, to shine; the skin of his face shone (Exo 34:29), the verb also meaning to send out horns.

Greek derma (G1192) — skin, hide; and dermatinos (G1193), made of skin, of the leathern girdle of John the Baptist.

Greek askos (G779) — a leathern bottle or wineskin; the old bottles which new wine would burst (Mat 9:17).

Usage

"Of the first covering God provided: unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make coats of skins, and clothed them (Gen 3:21)."

"Of the extremity of affliction: I am escaped with the skin of my teeth (Job 19:20)."

"Of the will's bondage: can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? (Jer 13:23)."
